title: Sunday Ticket
summary: Work out which four NFL games to put on the multiview, then watch every one of your players score on the same board.
body: Sunday Ticket answers one question: given every league you play in, which NFL games have the most of your players in them? It reads your rosters, works out where your starters actually are on a Sunday, and ranks the games so the four boxes on your multiview are the four worth having.

body.heading: Reading the board
items: Your matchup, up top. One card per league — your crest against your opponent's, both live scores, and how many starters each of you still has left to play. In both leagues, you get both cards.

Game boxes, below. One per NFL game in the window, ordered by how much of your roster is in it. Each player row shows his live fantasy points in that league's scoring, so the same player can carry two different numbers.
The Updated pill. When the board last actually heard from MFL. A board that says "live" and has not been confirmed since noon is not live, and the pill is how you tell.

body: The numbers refresh about once a minute while games are being played, then back off once everything is final. Lose your connection mid-afternoon and the scores you already have stay put rather than blanking out — a stale number with a timestamp on it beats a blank one.

body.heading: Two things it deliberately will not do
items: Leagues from outside this site show projections only. We can read your rosters there, but not their live scoring — those cards say Projections only rather than quietly showing you zeroes.
It is the wide shot, not the box score. For scoring plays, the ticker and the full breakdown, Live Scoring is still the deep cut.

body: Your country and clock preferences change what Sunday Ticket prints beside each game — kickoff times in your own clock, and the TV channel for where you actually live. Both are set on Preferences.

title: MFL Football
summary: Every team you own, in every MyFantasyLeague league, scoring on one page — then tap a league to see the whole thing: all its matchups, its standings, and the week's top scorers.
body: Every other scoreboard on this site shows you one league. MFL Football shows you all of them: sign in once with your MyFantasyLeague account and it reads every league that account plays in — this league, the other one, and the ones nobody here has ever heard of — then puts every matchup on a single page. It lives at its own address rather than under a league, because it does not belong to one.

body.heading: What's on the board
items: The NFL games strip, up top. The whole week's real games with live scores and clocks, so you can see what is still to come before you look at what it did to you.
One panel per league. Your matchup, both live totals, projected finals, how many starters each side has left, and a bar showing your share of the win. Doubleheader weeks show both games.

Tap a matchup for the lineups. Both teams, starters first in QB, RB, WR, TE, K, DEF order with several of a position grouped together, then the bench underneath with its own total — what you left on it, which is a different question from what you scored.

Scoring, across everything. A running list of every play that scored you points in any league. The same touchdown can appear more than once, and that is the point: one player started in three leagues really is three pieces of news.
Red zone. When one of your players' teams has the ball inside the twenty, it says so, and names who you have in the drive.

body.heading: Open the whole league
items: Tap a league's name at the top of its panel. The board you have been reading shows your own matchup; this opens that league's full board — every matchup in it, not just yours.
Your game still leads. The rest follow closest-first, so the game worth watching is the one at the top. Your own matchup is the only one badged, because most of the cards are nobody's.

Scores or Standings. Two buttons under the week. Standings are MyFantasyLeague's own table, in MyFantasyLeague's own order — records there update when games go final, not with the live scores beside them, and the table says so.

Top teams and top performances. Under the scores: who is putting up the week's numbers across the whole league, and the individual games behind it. Bench players never appear — those are points nobody can score.

body: This works for the outside leagues too — the ones this site does not run. Their standings and scores come straight from MyFantasyLeague with your own sign-in, so a league nobody here has heard of gets the same full board as this one.

body.heading: Crests and names
items: Teams in this league and the other one wear the crests you already know.

A team in an outside league whose name is a real NFL club — Cowboys, Chiefs, New Orleans Saints — gets that club's mark automatically. The match has to be exact, because a wrong crest is worse than none: The Boondock Saints is not the Saints.
Everyone else gets their initials. Nothing is guessed.

body: Switch leagues off in the board's own settings and it stops reading them altogether, which is what keeps a Sunday quick when you are in six of them. The choice is remembered on that device, so your phone and your laptop can watch different sets.

Scores refresh on their own while games are being played and ease off once everything is final. The pill beside the week number says when the board last actually heard from MyFantasyLeague — a page that says "live" but has not been confirmed in an hour is not live, and that is how you tell.

title: MFL Football on your TV
summary: Watch the broadcast board on any TV, and on Google TV put your score, win chance and lineups on top of the game you're watching.
body: There are two ways to watch on a TV. On a Google TV, the MFL Football app shows the full broadcast board and can also draw your scores over the game you're watching. On most other TVs and on Xbox, the TV's own web browser shows the same board, with no app to install.

body.heading: Which TV do you have?
items: Google TV or Android TV. This includes most Sony TVs, many TCL and Hisense TVs, and a Chromecast or Google TV Streamer. Use the app, below.
Fire TV, Samsung, LG or Xbox. Use the web browser. The steps are under Watch in your TV's browser.

Roku or Apple TV. These have no web browser and there's no MFL Football app for them yet. Plug a Google TV stick, such as the Google TV Streamer or an onn 4K stick, into a spare HDMI port and use the app.

Not sure? Press Home on the remote. The home screen names the system: Google TV, Fire TV, Roku, Tizen (Samsung), webOS (LG) or VIDAA (Hisense). VIDAA's browser hasn't been tested, so a Google TV stick is the safe choice there.

body: The MFL Football app on Google TV. Opened on its own, it shows the full broadcast board. Its score overlay (press Back in the app and pick Show scores) draws a small see-through score box in a corner of whatever you're watching, such as YouTube TV, so you can follow your matchups without leaving the game. The app is in testing right now, so getting it takes one extra step.

body.heading: Get the app
items: Send Brandon your TV's Google account. That's the Gmail address signed in on your Google TV. He adds you as a tester and sends you a link to join the test.
Join the test. Open that link on your phone or computer, signed in to the same Google account, and tap to join.
Install it. After a few hours, search the Play Store on your TV for MFL Football and install it.

body.heading: Set it up once
items: Sign in. Open MFL Football on the TV and point your phone's camera at the QR code. Sign in if it asks, then tap Approve. The TV switches to your board on its own.

Allow the overlay. In MFL Football, press Back and pick Show scores at the top. The first time, it asks to show over other apps: press OK and turn it on for MFL Football, then press Back. On some TVs the switch is under Settings › Apps › Special app access › Display over other apps.

No switch on your TV? The tile shows a one-line command instead. Run it once from a computer on the same Wi-Fi, with ADB installed and network debugging turned on in the TV's Developer options: adb shell appops set football.mfl.live SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow
Sunday Ticket. If you have NFL Sunday Ticket, tick I have NFL Sunday Ticket in MFL Football settings. The overlay then marks every Sunday afternoon CBS and FOX game as one you can open.

body.heading: While you watch
items: The full walkthrough. The TV score overlay covers every part of the overlay step by step, with pictures.

The score box. In MFL Football, press Back and pick Show scores at the top or at the bottom, then start your game in YouTube TV. A small see-through box in the corner shows your matchups one at a time, with team logos and a win bar, and the game's sound keeps playing. It never takes the remote, so your TV app keeps working.
Big plays. When one of your starters scores more than 3 points on a single play, the box grows for a few seconds with the player, the play and the new score.

Steer it from your phone. On the live board on your phone, tap TV remote: Quarter screen fills a corner with both lineups (made for multiview), Small shrinks it back, and Top, Bottom, Left and Right move it out of the way of the network's own graphics. The TV remembers where you put it.

The full panel. On TVs that show the Score overlay tile, open it again (or say "Open Score overlay") to open both lineups with the TV remote, then press OK for the panel: your score, win chance and both starting lineups.

Watch your players. The panel's Watch list shows the NFL games your starters are in, live games first. Up and Down pick a game and OK opens it on the TV through your TV's search, where you choose YouTube TV.

Back to the game. Back returns to the score box, and so does any other button, so the next press reaches your TV app. It also drops back to the score box after 30 seconds. To close the overlay altogether, open MFL Football, press Back and pick Turn off the score overlay.

body.heading: Watch in your TV's browser
items: Open the browser. On Samsung it's the Internet app. On LG it's Web Browser. On Fire TV it's Silk Browser; if it isn't on your home screen, search for Silk and install it, it's free. On Xbox it's Microsoft Edge, under My games & apps.
Go to mfl.football/tv. Type it into the address bar with the remote. A QR code appears.

Sign in with your phone. Point your phone's camera at the QR code, sign in if it asks, then tap Approve. The TV switches to the Broadcast page on its own. The TV only gets to watch; your sign-in stays on your phone.

Turn on sound first. Select Sound off next to the big button so it reads Sound on. A browser only plays sound after you've pressed something on the page, and that button isn't on screen once the board is full screen.

Go full screen. Select Go full screen. Back, or B on an Xbox controller, comes back out. If your browser can't do full screen, the same button opens the board on a page of its own that fills the screen instead.
Bookmark it. Add a bookmark for mfl.football/tv in the browser. Next time the board opens straight away, without the QR code.

body.heading: Browser tips
items: Keep the TV awake. The board asks the browser to keep the screen on, but not every TV browser listens, and none of them stops the TV's own power-off timer. Turn both off before kickoff to be safe. On Fire TV: Settings › Display & Sounds › Screensaver › Start Time › Never. On Samsung and LG, look for the screen saver and Auto Power Off settings, usually under General or Energy Saving. On Xbox: Settings › General › Power options.

Using the remote. The board runs on its own, so you don't need to touch it. To steer it with the TV remote, open mfl.football/live/broadcast?view=board on the TV, the board on a page of its own. There, Down takes the player strip at the bottom and Left and Right flip its pages, and Up picks a game in the header, where OK shows just that game's two rosters. Back returns to the full board.

Steer from your phone. Some TV browsers, and Edge on Xbox, move an on-screen pointer with the arrows instead of passing them to the page. Your phone works on any of them: open mfl.football/live/broadcast?view=board on the phone, tap TV remote and pick the TV.
Older TVs. Browsers on TVs from before about 2020 may be too old to draw the board properly. If yours shows a blank or broken page, a Google TV stick is the fix.

body: What the browser can't do. The score overlay over the game only works in the Google TV app, because a web page can't draw on top of another app. The browser shows the board on its own screen, so you switch between it and the game. A Google TV stick in any TV's HDMI port gets you the overlay.
The overlay and the browser board are still new, so tell Brandon what works on your TV and what doesn't.

title: The TV score overlay
summary: Keep your scores on screen while you watch the game on Google TV: a small see-through score box in a corner, a pop-out for your big plays, and a quarter-screen view for multiview.
body: The score overlay is part of the MFL Football app on Google TV. It draws a small, see-through score box in a corner of whatever you're watching, such as YouTube TV, NFL Sunday Ticket or a local channel, so your fantasy scores stay on screen without covering the game. The game's sound keeps playing the whole time. If you haven't installed the app yet, start with MFL Football on your TV.

body.alt: A football broadcast with the MFL Football score box in the upper right corner: the league's logo, both teams' logos and scores, and a win bar in the two teams' colors.
body.caption: The score box in the upper right, clear of the network's score banner at the bottom.

body.heading: Turn it on
items: Which TVs. The overlay needs the MFL Football app, so it works on Google TV and Android TV: most Sony TVs, many TCL, Hisense and Philips TVs, a Chromecast with Google TV, a Google TV Streamer or an Nvidia Shield. Fire TV, Samsung and LG don't let one app draw over another, so use the Broadcast board in your TV's browser there instead. Roku has no browser at all; plug a Google TV stick into a spare HDMI port and use the overlay on that. MFL Football on your TV covers both.

Open MFL Football and press Back. On the board, press Back until a menu asks Keep your scores on screen? Pick Show scores at the top or Show scores at the bottom. The app closes and the score box appears over the home screen.
Then start the game. Open YouTube TV, or whatever you watch on, and start the game. The score box stays on top and the game's sound plays as normal.

Start the overlay before the game. Pressing Home while a game plays sends the game to the background, so turn the scores on first. If the game is already on, press Home, turn the scores on, then go back into your TV app; the game picks up where it was.

The first time only. The TV asks to let MFL Football show over other apps. Press OK, turn it on, then press Back. If it doesn't ask, or you said no, turn it on yourself: Settings › Apps › Special app access › Display over other apps (on Sony and most Google TVs; some TVs call it Appear on top, and older ones keep it under Apps › Security & restrictions). Find MFL Football in the list and switch it to Allowed. The setup steps in MFL Football on your TV cover TVs without that switch.
No menu? If Back just closes the app, your TV has an older version. Update MFL Football from the Play Store.

body.alt: The TV's Allow display over other apps settings screen, with MFL Football switched on and marked Allowed.
body.caption: Settings › Apps › Special app access › Display over other apps on a Sony TV. MFL Football should say Allowed.

body.heading: The Score overlay tile and voice
items: A shortcut on some TVs. MFL Football also installs a Score overlay tile. Most Google TV home screens show only one tile per app and hide it, but some Android TVs (Nvidia Shield, older Sony and Philips TVs, Android TV boxes) list it under Apps. If yours does, opening it turns the ticker on without leaving your game.

Voice. Hold the voice button on the remote and say "Open Score overlay". Whether this works depends on the TV finding that tile; if it opens a search or the MFL Football board instead, use the Back menu.
Pin it. If you can see the tile, highlight it, hold OK and pick Add to favorites (or Move) to keep it on the home screen.

body.heading: Reading the score box
items: One matchup at a time. The box shows the league's logo, then your team's logo and score, a win bar, and your opponent's score and logo. The leading score is gold.
The win bar. Your team's color fills your chance to win and your opponent's color fills the rest. Once a game is decided, the loser's color disappears.
It rotates. If you're in more than one league, or have two games in a doubleheader week, the box moves to the next one every 8 seconds. The dots on the right show which one you're on.
It never takes the remote. Every button press still goes to your TV app, so you can pause, rewind and change channels as usual.

body.alt: The score box grown into the upper right quarter of the screen: Big play, Bijan Robinson with the Falcons logo, plus 7.2 points, counting in both leagues, above the matchup's new score.
body.caption: A big play by one of your starters grows the box for a few seconds.

body.heading: Big plays
items: Only your players. When one of your own starters scores more than 3 fantasy points on a single play, the box grows into its quarter of the screen with a Big play card. Your opponent's players never trigger one.

What it shows. The player's headshot on his team's color (or his team's logo when there's no headshot) and name, what happened when the play-by-play has it ("48 Yd pass from Sam Darnold"), the points it was worth, and your matchup's new score along the top.
Several leagues. If you start the same player in more than one league, you get one card, with a Counts in row showing each league's logo.
Timing. The card shows up when the fantasy scoring updates, usually within a minute of the play, and stays for about 7 seconds before the box shrinks back. Several big plays at once take turns.

body.alt: A YouTube TV multiview with three games in three quarters of the screen and the MFL Football quarter view in the fourth: both starting lineups with each player's points, and the other matchups along the bottom.
body.caption: Quarter screen: your fantasy matchup takes the spare quarter of a multiview.

body.heading: Quarter screen, for multiview
items: Fill a whole quarter. When YouTube TV's multiview shows three games and you don't need the fourth, put your fantasy scores there. On your phone, open the live board at mfl.football/live/broadcast (signed in, as the owner who paired the TV), tap TV remote and pick Quarter screen. Small puts the score box back.

What's in it. Both starting lineups with each player's points. A green dot marks who is playing right now, and players whose games are over are dimmed. Your other matchups sit along the bottom, and the main one changes every 20 seconds. Next game on your phone moves it sooner.
Big plays here. The player's row lights up in gold instead of a pop-out.
It stays. Quarter screen stays up until you pick Small, even after the TV restarts the overlay. Your TV remote keeps working on the show the whole time.

body.alt: The same broadcast with the network's score banner at the top of the screen, and the MFL Football score box moved to the lower left corner to stay out of its way.
body.caption: When the network's graphics are in the way, move the box to another corner.

body.heading: Move it to another corner
items: From your phone. On the live board on your phone (mfl.football/live/broadcast), open TV remote and tap Top, Bottom, Left or Right. You can also open MFL Football on the TV, press Back and pick Move scores to the top or bottom.
Pick the clear corner. Most networks put their score banner along the bottom, so the upper right is usually best, but some broadcasts and streaming apps use the top.
It remembers. The TV keeps your choice, so the box comes back in the same corner next time.

body.heading: The full panel and Watch list
items: Open the Score overlay again on a TV that shows its tile to open both lineups with the TV remote, then press OK to bring up the full panel down the left side: your score, win chance, projections and both starting lineups.

Watch your players. The panel's Watch list shows the NFL games your starters are in, live games first. Up and Down pick a game and OK opens it through your TV's search, where you choose your TV app. With I have NFL Sunday Ticket ticked in MFL Football settings, every Sunday afternoon CBS and FOX game is marked as one you can open.
Back returns to the ticker.

body.heading: Turn it off
items: From the Back menu. Open MFL Football, press Back and pick Turn off the score overlay.
Or from the full panel. With the full panel open, go to the bottom of the Watch list and pick Hide overlay.
Or turn off the TV. The overlay closes by itself when the screen goes off.

body: The overlay is new, so tell Brandon what works on your TV and what doesn't.
